summary: Phase 1 HA Foundation — comprehensive backend testing completed. 35/35 new tests pass (100%) covering branches CRUD + role gates + primary-branch invariant + soft-delete, vendors CRUD + search + special-char safety + role gates (including newly-provisioned inventory_manager), auth.branch_ids in both /auth/login and /auth/me, the numbering helper (PO-YYYY-NNNN year-reset + per-clinic isolation), the 9-state SerialItem state machine (complete STATES set + legal/illegal transitions + transition_serial audit-row atomicity — illegal transition correctly does NOT emit an audit row), cross-tenant isolation (Delhi admin cannot see Mumbai branches or GET by id), and seed idempotency (no duplicate Mumbai HQ / Delhi branch; exactly one primary per clinic). 27/27 iter12 regression tests still pass — zero regressions against the prior green baseline. Grand total: 62/62 backend tests green.
critical_code_review_comments: branches.py POST uses `require_roles('clinic_owner')` which includes super_admin via the `{'super_admin'}` union in require_roles() — correct, but role list is implicit. Consider explicit `require_roles('clinic_owner', 'super_admin')` for readability (super_admin override is easy to miss by future reviewers).

numbering.py: the counter doc on first call uses upsert + $inc which returns the PRE-increment doc when return_document=True isn't ReturnDocument.AFTER. Currently `return_document=True` works because motor treats truthy as AFTER, but this is brittle — prefer `from pymongo import ReturnDocument; return_document=ReturnDocument.AFTER` for clarity.

ha_states.py RETURNED is declared terminal-ish (→ RETIRED only) but has no path back to IN_STOCK; architecturally fine per spec but worth documenting that a returned unit cannot be re-stocked — vendor credit is the only exit.

branches.py update_branch: when payload.is_primary is False but the record being edited IS currently primary, the user could accidentally leave the clinic with ZERO primaries. Invariant is 'at most one' — consider enforcing 'exactly one' (reject demoting the sole primary, or auto-promote another).

Soft-deleted branches (active=false) are still returned by GET /api/branches/{id} and update_branch/delete_branch operate on them — the GET single-branch handler does not filter by active. Minor; may be intentional for audit UI but worth a comment.

server.py _seed_primary_branch runs on every boot; the `find_one({is_primary:true})` check works but is not atomic vs. concurrent boots (multi-replica deployments could race and create two primaries). Unique partial index on (clinic_id, is_primary=true) would harden this.

vendors.py search: the `re.escape(search.strip())` is correct against regex-special chars (we tested $.^) but the $or still runs four separate regex OR clauses against name/contact_person/phone/email — at scale this should be a text index; low priority for Phase 1.

auth.require_roles auto-grants super_admin via `set(roles) | {'super_admin'}` — this is correct but should also grant clinic_owner for most write endpoints (currently it does NOT — every writer must explicitly list clinic_owner). Vendors does; consistency check across future modules.
test_credentials: admin@acs.in/admin123, frontdesk@acs.in/frontdesk123, admin@delhi.test/delhiadmin123; provisioned test_inv@acs.in/invpass123 (inventory_manager) directly via motor insert — deleted at test end.
seed_data_creation: Test run transiently creates: (a) one inventory_manager user `test_inv@acs.in` in clinic-acs-demo (cleaned up in test_cleanup_vendors), (b) test counters with _id prefixes `po:TEST_A:` and `po:TEST_B:` (cleaned up before re-use), (c) test serial item TEST_SERIAL_PHASE1 + its serial_events rows (cleaned up at end of test_transition_serial_writes_audit). Transient branches/vendors are soft-deleted during the run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 1 foundation is green and locked. The new regression surface for all future HA phases: /api/branches (full CRUD + primary invariant), /api/vendors (full CRUD + search + special-char safety), auth payload includes branch_ids, utils/numbering.next_number, utils/ha_states.{STATES,ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS,assert_transition,transition_serial}, and the Mumbai HQ + Delhi primary-branch seed invariants. Re-use /app/backend/tests/test_phase1_ha_foundation.py as-is for regression in Phase 2+. Note: server.py has WatchFiles hot-reload on /app/backend/tests changes — triggers brief 1-2s reload. Login endpoint lowercases email (req.email.strip().lower()), so any directly-inserted test users MUST store email in lowercase or login returns 401.
rca of the issue: No phase-1 issues identified. Two test-authoring bugs self-fixed during test run: (a) initially inserted user with email 'TEST_inv@acs.in' (mixed case) but login endpoint normalizes to lowercase — fixed by using 'test_inv@acs.in'; (b) /closeouts/current returns 404 when no close-out exists for today which is expected behavior — test expectation loosened to accept 200 OR 404.
